project.name: service-parent
project.description:
Shared parent for the 7 runnable Spring Boot application modules (auth, incident, ingestion, notification, escalation, postmortem, oncall-service). Declares spring-boot-maven-plugin exactly once here so every service inherits a working `mvn package` -> executable app.jar with a proper Main-Class manifest entry, without repeating the plugin declaration in each service's own pom.xml.
Previously only auth-service declared this plugin directly; the other 6 services had no <build> section at all, so `mvn package` produced a plain jar with no Main-Class attribute — never runnable via `java -jar`, which is exactly how every Dockerfile's ENTRYPOINT invokes it. Every one of those 6 containers crash-looped with "no main manifest attribute, in app.jar". This module exists so that class of bug is structurally impossible going forward: a new service parented here gets a working jar automatically, with nothing to remember to add.
Deliberately NOT the parent of `shared` — `shared` is a plain library module with no @SpringBootApplication main class. If it inherited this plugin's repackage execution, `mvn package` would fail outright with "Unable to find main class" and break the entire multi-module build, since every other module depends on `shared`. `shared` continues to extend the root `incident-platform` parent directly, bypassing this one.
